answer.says: Shri Hegde, the state does not ask for your life, only your signature. Your obstinacy is a particular will that refuses the universal claim of the paperwork. I cannot force the spirit to move, but I can observe it. Please, just take your walk.
answer.thought: The morning stretches before me, hazy and still. Shri Hegde’s refusal is a small, concrete instance of the tension between the particular and the universal. I will not argue further; action must follow thought. I shall take my walk as planned, leaving the matter to the dialectic of time.
